title: iOS 27: What’s new, what’s in the latest beta and what’s coming next
content:
Macworld





Apple unveiled iOS 27 at WWDC on June 8, 2026, with the public release following on September 14. The latest update, iOS 27.2, arrived on October 26, bringing further Siri AI improvements and new app features. More additions are still to come.
iOS 27 mainly focuses on three key areas: Siri AI, a rebuilt assistant with its own dedicated app; new child safety and parental controls; and system improvements designed to make everyday tasks faster and easier.
iOS 27 supports the iPhone 11 and later, plus the iPhone SE (2nd generation) and later, although some Apple Intelligence and Siri features require newer hardware.
This guide covers iOS 27’s biggest new features, compatible iPhones, the latest beta developments and the promised features still to come in future updates.


What’s New in iOS 27 at a Glance
Siri AI: Apple’s new Siri AI combines personal context, onscreen awareness and web knowledge to deliver more natural conversations, richer answers, app actions and cross-device chat history.
Apple Intelligence across apps: Apple Intelligence expands across Safari, Photos, Messages, Mail, Calendar, Home and Shortcuts, adding smarter suggestions, automation, image generation and context-aware assistance.
Smarter Photos editing: Photos gains Spatial Reframing, Extend and an upgraded Clean Up tool, allowing users to improve composition, expand images and remove distractions more naturally.
Child safety and parental controls: New parental controls include Ask to Browse, Time Allowances, app schedules and enhanced Communication Safety tools. Activating the redesigned experience through Family Sharing requires every eligible family device to be running version 27 or later.
System Improvements: Apple has made many system operations faster and more efficient, which will be especially noticeable on older phones. Battery life may be longer, and there are dozens of small quality-of-life improvements throughout the system and its apps.
iPhone Handoff: iPhone Handoff in iOS 27 lets two eSIM-equipped iPhones share one number, switching calls, messages and Find My location when unlocked. It requires matching Apple Accounts and carrier support. T-Mobile offers it; Verizon and EE plan support. Fees may apply. More information below.


						

							


iOS 27 latest version: What’s in iOS 27.2
Apple released iOS 27.2 on October 26, 2026. It improves Siri AI’s memory and personal context, expands language support, and adds Suggestions in Messages alongside other app improvements, bug fixes and security updates. Dual Capture arrives for Group FaceTime calls, while iPhone Duo gains Apple Pencil (USB-C) support and Edge Light to illuminate your face during video calls. Shared Albums in Photos gains editable captions and comments, helps avoid duplicate photos, and provides reminders to save photos and videos before temporary albums expire. Read our iOS 27.2 guide for more details.
iOS 27 version history: Every update and release date
The first update was iOS 27.0.1, released on September 28. It fixed unexpected restarts following failed Face ID authentication, a 2x-camera color artifact affecting iPhone 18 Pro models, and an iOS 27 touchscreen freeze triggered by opening Notification Center and Control Center simultaneously.
iOS 27.0.1 also has a preventive role in a cellular problem that Apple did not mention in its published release notes. Apple has confirmed that a small number of iPhone 18 Pro Max models on AT&T can lose cellular service, preventing calls, texts and data access and potentially affecting 911 calls. Some owners reported their phones dropping into SOS mode despite previously showing a strong 5G signal.
Apple released iOS 27.2 on October 26, 2026. Details above. 


						

							


iOS 27 beta – What’s coming next?
Latest developer beta: iOS 27.3 beta 1, released November 3, 2026.
Apple has begun testing iOS 27.3. Changes reported in the first version of the developer beta include:
Redesigned Health app: The new design returns after appearing briefly during iOS 27.2 testing.
Apple Watch Audio Intelligence: Live Rewind and Siri Recap are available for testing with an Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4.
More Siri AI languages: Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish and Vietnamese are being tested.
Expanded Siri actions: Siri gains more capabilities within Apple’s apps, while developers can begin testing new integrations for third-party apps.
Apple Intelligence in China: Initial features include Writing Tools, Visual Intelligence, Clean Up and Genmoji. Siri AI remains unavailable.
iPhone Duo Reachability: Content can shift sideways to make the wider display easier to reach.


						

							


What features are still to come in iOS 27
At the time of the launch of iOS 27 not all of Apple’s promised features were available. Several were added in iOS 27.2, but there are still a couple that we’re waiting on.
Redesigned Health app: The new Health app has returned in the iOS 27.3 developer beta.
Automatic password changes: The ability for the Passwords app to visit supported websites and automatically replace compromised passwords was removed shortly before release. 


						

							


What does Siri AI do in iOS 27

				
					

				
			
Apple




By far the biggest upgrade in iOS 27 is Siri AI – an entirely new architecture for Siri. Apple says it is more personal, conversational, and capable than the current assistant, with support for natural follow-up questions, personal context, onscreen awareness and up-to-date information from the web.
Siri AI features
More natural conversations: Siri AI can understand open-ended questions, follow-up requests and more complex natural language, making interactions feel less like issuing simple voice commands.
Personal context: Siri can draw on information stored in Messages, Mail, Photos and Notes to find details and answer questions. For example, you could ask it to find information buried in an old email or message.
Onscreen awareness: Siri can understand what you’re viewing and act on it, such as saving an address from a message, adding an event to Calendar or answering questions about an article.
Camera intelligence: A new Siri Camera mode lets you show Siri something through the iPhone’s camera, then ask questions or perform actions based on what it sees.
More capable app actions: Siri can perform tasks within apps such as Messages, Music and Reminders. It can, for example, edit a recently sent message, add a song to a playlist or handle more complex Apple Music requests.
Better general knowledge and web answers: Siri can use information from the web to answer questions about recent events and tackle more specific or complicated queries than before.
Conversation history across devices: A dedicated Siri app lets users revisit previous conversations, pin important chats and continue conversations across Apple devices using iCloud syncing.
More natural Siri voices: Siri gains more expressive voices, with controls on compatible devices for adjusting speaking pace and expressiveness. Voice customization requires an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air or newer.
Improved dictation: Better speech recognition, automatic punctuation, capitalization and formatting allow users to dictate more naturally when converting speech into text.
AI-assisted message replies: Siri can compose contextual replies in Messages using the conversation, personal information and web searches. Shortcuts can also automate replies to selected contacts, although manual Siri-assisted replies allow users to check and edit the response before it is sent.
iOS 27.2 added several further Siri AI improvements:
Recall information from previous conversations.
Use Messages photo attachments, Calendar attendees and voicemails, with better results from Safari history and Reading List.
Control app access for Siri, Search and suggestions through Excluded Apps.
Select and copy individual portions of Siri’s responses.
iOS 27.3 expands Siri’s actions across Apple apps, including Calendar, Messages, Music and Reminders. You can ask Siri what it can do within an app.
Apple has also opened a developer preview that lets third-party apps connect their content and actions to Siri AI. This requires developers to build support into their apps. Apple says App Store submissions using these capabilities will open in spring, so installing iOS 27.3 alone will not enable the new integrations across existing apps.
If you haven’t got Siri AI yet find out how here: Why don’t I have Siri AI on my iPhone?
Read about what happened when we made Siri AI Answer all our Messages.
How good is Siri AI?
Siri AI represents a significant improvement over the old Siri, particularly when handling conversational questions, current information, and personal context. It also has a dedicated app where you can see and continue previous conversations, upload images or documents, and more.
Even in our early tests during the beta, Siri AI proved to be much more helpful and useful. 
It’s definitely one of the biggest reasons to upgrade to iOS 27, potentially changing Siri from a basic voice-command system into a more general way of interacting with the iPhone.
Apple’s approach to AI safety also appears more restrained than some rival chatbots, with Siri designed to avoid excessive flattery, pretending to be human, or responding inappropriately to potentially harmful requests.
Siri AI remains a beta feature. iOS 27.2 added French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish alongside English. Siri AI remains unavailable on iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch in the EU and mainland China. The EU restriction does not apply to Siri AI on Mac so Siri AI can be used on the Mac in the EU.
Regional Siri AI availability
Siri AI will not initially be available on iPhone or iPad in the EU. It will also remain unavailable in China while Apple works through regulatory issues. 
The first release only supported the English language, and initially had only Expressive Voices for English (UK) and English (US). Support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish arrived with iOS 27.2. 
Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish and Vietnamese support is being tested in the iOS 27.3 beta. Siri AI is still not available in mainland China.
Lack of Siri language support is separate to Apple Intelligence language support. 
Siri AI compatibility
Siri AI requires iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, and all iPhone 16 models and later, and the “new expressive voices” feature requires an iPhone 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max, iPhone Air, iPhone 18 Pro or 18 Pro Max and currently supports US and UK English voices.
Siri AI age restriction: Siri AI is unavailable to children under 13.


						

							


Apple Intelligence across apps
As well as Siri AI, the enhanced Apple Intelligence will power new features in Apple’s core apps throughout iOS 27. Safari can organize tabs into topics, monitor webpages for changes and even build extensions from natural-language descriptions. Photos gains a new Spatial Reframing editing tools including an upgraded Clean Up feature. Messages, Mail, and Calendar can now understand context, suggest actions and create events from simple descriptions.
Usage limits: Some cloud-based Apple Intelligence features have daily limits. The limits cover Siri AI as well as other cloud-based Apple Intelligence features, including intelligent photo editing, Image Playground and cloud models in Shortcuts. Apple says expanded access will be available for a fee in future.


						

							


New features coming to apps in iOS 27
iOS 27 brings a mix of major Apple Intelligence upgrades and smaller quality-of-life improvements across Safari, Photos, Messages, AirPods, Passwords, Wallet, and other core iPhone apps. Apple is also making iOS more adaptable to different screen sizes and orientations, which are changes necessary for the iPhone Duo.
Safari
Safari can automatically group open tabs into topics, making related pages easier to find. A new Notify Me feature will monitor webpages and alert you to changes such as price drops or products coming back into stock.
There’s also a new Describe an Extension feature which lets users create custom Safari extensions simply by explaining what they want the extension to do.

				
					

				
			

Apple




Photos
Photos gains significantly more powerful AI editing tools.
Reframe can alter the composition and perspective of an existing photo, while Extend generates new image content beyond the original frame when straightening a horizon or changing the aspect ratio.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Clean Up has also been improved, with Fast and High Quality modes for removing unwanted objects or details. High Quality mode can produce considerably more natural results, although more ambitious edits can still introduce distortions or invented details.
Photos also adds new categories and the ability to save a frame from a video as a full-resolution photo. The resulting HEIF or JPG retains the video’s original resolution, date, and location metadata rather than simply creating a screenshot.
Camera
iOS 27 features a new more customizable camera interface that lets you pin the controls you use most often. For the iPhone 18 Pro, there are also “pro controls” like white balance, shutter speed, and manual focus along with Apple Reference Image, an authentication system designed to prove that a photo or video was genuinely captured on an iPhone and has not subsequently been manipulated.
The new Siri mode in the Camera app is a more convenient and logical way to access the Visual Intelligence features that used to require either a long-press of the camera button or a Control Center button.
Messages

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Messages gets several useful improvements.
You can decide what the microphone button beside the text field does. Under Settings > Apps > Messages > Show in Text Field, it can be set to Record Audio, Start Dictation, or None. Disabling it does not remove either feature: dictation remains available from the keyboard and audio messages remain in the + menu.
Voice-message playback controls are easier to access. 
iOS 27.2 adds Suggestions in Messages, which uses the context of your conversations to suggest actions in apps such as Calendar and Reminders. For example, when you discuss dinner plans, Messages can suggest creating a Calendar invitation.
Messages in iOS 27 will gain smarter suggested replies that can better reflect the user’s writing style. (This was removed from the iOS 27 beta and wasn’t available at the launch of iOS 27).
Drawing

				
					

				
			
Foundry




A new dedicated Drawing app replaces the old hidden handwriting interface. Accessible from the + menu, it uses the familiar pens, colours and drawing controls found in Notes and Markup, with finished drawings sent as images.
Mail
Mail gains more context-aware smart replies, including responses that can better match the user’s usual writing style.
Apple Intelligence can also surface information from Mail elsewhere in iOS. For example, the Phone app could retrieve a flight confirmation number from an email when you call an airline.
Phone
A new Call Context feature can surface information that may be useful when on a call. Apple says the information is selected according to who you are calling rather than by listening to the conversation. For example, calling an airline could cause iOS to surface the relevant flight confirmation from Mail.
Birthday reminders can also appear when calling contacts whose birthdays are stored on the iPhone.
iPhone Handoff
iPhone Handoff in iOS 27 lets you switch between two iPhones while keeping the same phone number. The number is active on only one iPhone at a time. When you unlock one of the two iPhones, your calls, voicemail, messages—including SMS and RCS—and your Find My location will be linked to that iPhone. 
The feature will work on any iPhone running iOS 27, as long as it has an eSIM. Both phones must use the same Apple Account, with Messages in iCloud enabled and matching FaceTime/iMessage sign-ins. 
You will need a carrier and eligible plan that specifically support iPhone Handoff – an ordinary eSIM plan alone isn’t enough. In the U.S. T-Mobile offers iPhone Handoff for $5 a month and Verizon has announced support for later in 2026. In the U.K. EE has announced that support for iPhone Handoff is coming soon for £5 a month. 
FaceTime
Dual Capture arrived in iOS 27.2, allowing Group FaceTime participants to share front- and rear-camera views simultaneously. 
iOS 27.2 also adds support for bringing a third-party sign language interpreter or live captioner into a FaceTime call, providing additional communication support for participants.
Passwords

				
					

				
			
Passwords in iOS 27 will fix things for you.

Apple




The Passwords app continues to warn about weak, reused and compromised credentials, but iOS 27 will go a step further – eventually. Automatic password changes are coming to the Passwords app in a future software update. Apple has not confirmed a release date.
The forthcoming feature will, with your permission, visit supported websites, change vulnerable passwords and save the replacement credentials automatically. See: Apple got rid of my biggest password headache.
The usefulness of the feature will depend on how widely websites are supported and how well it handles obstacles such as two-factor authentication and unusual account-management interfaces. 
Apple removed this ability to detect compromised passwords and replace them from the beta shortly before the release of iOS 27. It’s expected to arrive with a later update.
Shortcuts
Shortcuts gains Describe a Shortcut, allowing users to create automations simply by explaining what they want to happen.
Apple Intelligence interprets the request and assembles the appropriate actions across supported apps, potentially making Shortcuts significantly easier to use for people unfamiliar with building automations manually.
Calendar
Calendar can create or modify events from natural-language instructions.
Apple says the app can recognize contacts, locations, dates and other event details as users type, reducing the amount of information that needs to be entered manually.
Siri can also create complete Calendar entries for information that is on your screen in that moment, or by taking a picture with the Siri mode in the Camera app.
Image Playground
Image Playground is considerably more powerful and realistic.
Apple says it can create photorealistic images and lets users modify generated pictures simply by describing the changes they want. Individual objects can also be selected, resized, or repositioned.
iOS 27.2 adds SynthID support to help identify images generated or modified using Photos and Image Playground.
Wallet
Wallet can create custom passes from QR codes.
Users can add their own fields and information to the pass, and passes automatically sync to Apple Watch.
Weather
Weather gets a clearer, more detailed forecast interface, with rearranged information tiles and new 10-day views showing precipitation probability/amount and wind speed throughout each day.
Home app
Apple Intelligence comes to the Home app for compatible HomeKit Secure Video cameras. It can group related camera notifications, describe recorded video and highlight clips that appear particularly noteworthy.
Maps
Apple Maps improves Flyover using higher-quality aerial imagery and Visual Intelligence models.
Apple says this produces sharper architectural detail and more realistic rendering of elements such as individual trees.
Podcasts
Video podcasts become easier to use, with improved controls for switching between watching a podcast and simply listening to it.
iOS 27.2 also reorganizes the Podcasts app’s Home tab into two separate sections: New Episodes, where you can find the latest releases from shows you follow, and Continue Playing, where you can resume episodes you’ve already started. This makes it easier to distinguish new listening from unfinished episodes.
Fitness
Workout summaries have been redesigned to make them easier to share.
Users can also hide completed Fitness+ workouts.
Games 
iOS 27.2 improves the Games app’s Friends tab with more information about suggested friends. Friends’ player pages also show the games they’ve played recently, making it easier to find something to play together.
Apple TV 
iOS 27.2 adds Simple Profiles to the Apple TV app, allowing members of your household to have their own profiles with recommendations tailored to their viewing preferences.


						

							


iOS 27 changes beyond the iPhone 
CarPlay
CarPlay gains an audio scrubber, giving drivers and passengers more direct control when moving through audio tracks and other content.
AirPods
iOS 27 introduces several new AirPods features.
A new Custom EQ lets users independently adjust bass, mids and treble using a simple three-band equalizer under Settings > AirPods > Audio and Routing > Equalizer > Custom.
Compatible AirPods also gain improved Precision Finding through Find My, making individual earbuds easier to locate.
Some features require both iOS 27 and compatible AirPods firmware.
Read How to tune your AirPods with a custom EQ in iOS 27.


						

							


Other changes in iOS 27
It’s not only individual apps that are seeing changes.
Home Screen and landscape mode
Apple is making iOS significantly more flexible when dealing with different screen orientations and sizes.
More Apple apps now work properly in landscape, including Health, Home, Music, Weather, and Watch. Dynamic Island and Live Activities can also adapt to landscape orientation. The Home Screen supports extra-large widgets.
These changes could simply improve iPhone usability, but they’re also well suited to Apple’s folding iPhone Duo.
iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 has similarly become freely resizable, with Apple apps dynamically rearranging their interfaces as the window changes shape.
Liquid Glass refinements

				
					

				
			
Apple




Apple says Liquid Glass has been refined for better readability, more uniform refraction and improved contrast. A new slider lets users adjust the look from ultraclear to fully tinted, while updated icons, toolbars, sidebars and window shapes add polish.
Ringtones, alarms and alert volume
iOS 27 finally separates several sound-volume controls.
Instead of one combined Ringtone and Alerts slider, users can independently adjust:
Ringtones
Alarms and timers
Alerts and system sounds
The change is optional. Under Settings > Sounds & Haptics, turning off Match Ringtone Volume reveals separate controls.
Media and call volume continue to work independently as before.
Keyboard
iOS 27 introduces a new quick-paste control above the keyboard.
It lets you paste recently copied text, images or screenshots without having to long-press inside a text field, making everyday copy-and-paste considerably faster.
Apple has also made the Liquid Glass keyboard design more consistent across apps.
Privacy and Find My
iOS 27 introduces the ability to temporarily pause Find My location sharing without notifying the person with whom the location is normally shared.
Recovery and troubleshooting
Apple is also expanding the iPhone’s recovery interface, giving users more options for diagnosing problems and recovering an iPhone without immediately connecting it to another device.


						

							


System changes and how iOS 27 makes your iPhone faster
Alongside the headline AI features, Apple says iOS 27 includes a wide range of under-the-hood improvements designed to make iPhones faster, smoother and more efficient.
Apps can launch up to 30% faster, newly taken photos can appear in the Photos library up to 70% faster, and AirDrop transfers can be up to 80% quicker. External drive transfers should also improve, while updates to network performance and the system-wide search index are designed to make connectivity and finding information faster.
The company has also reworked core technologies including CPU scheduling, display performance and processing efficiency. These changes should benefit older iPhones in particular, with Apple promising smoother performance and more efficient battery use on devices as old as the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE.
Our testing of the iOS 27 beta supports those claims. On an iPhone 11 Pro Max, Camera launch time fell from 0.98 seconds in iOS 26 to 0.65 seconds in iOS 27, while Maps improved from 3.01 seconds to 1.36 seconds.
Everyday use also feels smoother, with more fluid animations, unlocking, Control Center and app transitions. The phone ran cooler during testing too, which could point to improved system efficiency and potentially better battery performance.
More broadly, iOS 27 appears focused on refinement rather than simply adding new features. Apple says it has addressed dozens of common user frustrations, while changes such as more adjustable Liquid Glass effects are intended to improve readability and general usability.
That focus should make iOS 27 particularly worthwhile for owners of older iPhones, even on models that do not support Siri AI. Those devices still gain performance improvements alongside features such as clipboard tools for the keyboard, independent alarm and timer volume controls, custom Wallet passes, Photos changes, larger widgets, and Liquid Glass refinements.


						

							


Child safety and parental controls

				
					

				
			
Apple




There are lots of improvements to parental controls, including new time allowances for entertainment, games, and social media, and new schedule tools for different times of day or days of the week.
This includes new features like an expansion of the existing “ask to buy” feature for apps to websites. Before a child can view a new website, they’ll have to ask for permission.
Ask to Browse: Will expand the current Ask to Buy feature to the web. Children will need to request permission before visiting new websites, and parents can review requests in Messages before approving.
Communication Safety: Communication Safety continues to help protect children from viewing or sharing nudity in Messages, FaceTime and other apps. Apple says it will also intervene before children see gore or violent content in shared images and videos.
Time Allowances and schedules: Parents can set Time Allowances across categories such as Entertainment, Games and Social Media. Recommendations are based on a child’s age combined with guidance from clinical and child development experts. Schedules let parents choose which apps are available at different times or on different days.
Redesigned Screen Time: Screen Time gets a redesigned interface with an at-a-glance view of average device usage and most-used apps. Apple says parents can quickly limit or extend access in the moment.
Child accounts and family safety: Apple says child accounts remain central to age-appropriate protections. Parents can manage app access, web access, communication permissions and Screen Time settings. 
Problems with Parental Control setup
Updating the parent’s iPhone is not enough to activate the redesigned Screen Time experience. Apple says every eligible iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch and Vision Pro in the Family Sharing group must be running the appropriate version 27 software.
Devices that cannot run version 27 are listed as Legacy Devices and can continue using the older Screen Time and Family Sharing system. Apple says these incompatible devices should not prevent supported devices from adopting the new controls.
To find out which devices need to be updated go to Settings > Family > View Family Devices. Once eligible devices are running iOS 27, go to Settings > Family > Get Started to transfer the family’s existing parental controls or set up new ones.
Some families have encountered delays, outdated device listings and eligible hardware incorrectly appearing not to have been updated. Apple has acknowledged the rollout problems and says it is working to resolve them. If an eligible device is no longer owned or accessible, Apple recommends removing it from the Apple Account device list.


						

							


Accessibility changes in iOS 27
Accessibility features are smarter and more intuitive in iOS 27:
VoiceOver gives richer image descriptions and better understanding of onscreen content.
Live Recognition lets users press the Action button to ask questions about their surroundings and receive detailed responses.
Voice Control is more intuitive, allowing users to describe onscreen buttons and controls rather than remembering exact coordinate labels or numbers.
Accessibility Reader is able to handle more complex source material and provide summaries and translation.


						

							


iOS 27 compatibility 

				
					

				
			iPhone 11 is supported by iOS 27.
Roman Loyola/IDG




According to Apple, iOS 27 supports iPhones back to the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE, although some Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features require newer hardware.
Support for iOS 27 does not mean every device gets every feature. Apple Intelligence and Siri AI require an iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 16 or later, while the most advanced on-device AI models require an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air, or iPhone 18 Pro. On iPad, Apple Intelligence requires an M1-class model or the A17 Pro iPad mini, while the newest on-device models require an M4 iPad with at least 12GB of RAM.
There had been speculation that the iPhone 11 series and iPhone SE 2 would miss out on iOS 27 after leaker Instant Digital claimed on Weibo that the 2019 iPhone 11, 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max, along with the 2020 iPhone SE 2, would no longer be supported. That prediction proved incorrect, giving those models at least one more year of software support.
However, the iPhone 11 generation is nearing the end of its support life. As we explain in our guide to how long Apple supports iPhones, the iPhone 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max have already been added to Apple’s Vintage iPhone list.
The iOS 27 compatibility list is:
iPhone 18 Pro
iPhone 18 Pro Max
iPhone Duo
iPhone 17e (launched in 2026) 
iPhone 17, 17 Pro / 17 Pro Max (launched in 2025)
iPhone Air (launched in 2025)
iPhone 16e (launched in 2025)
iPhone 16 / 16 Plus and iPhone 16 Pro / 16 Pro Max (launched in 2024)
iPhone 15 / 15 Plus and iPhone 15 Pro / 15 Pro Max (launched in 2023)
iPhone 14 / 14 Plus / 14 Pro / 14 Pro Max (launched in 2022)
iPhone SE 3 (launched in 2022)
iPhone 13 / 13 mini / 13 Pro / 13 Pro Max (launched in 2021)
iPhone 12 / 12 mini / 12 Pro / 12 Pro Max (launched in 2020)
iPhone SE 2 (launched in 2020)
iPhone 11 / 11 Pro / 11 Pro Max (launched in 2019)
The main dividing line for Apple Intelligence remains the iPhone 15 Pro generation: the standard iPhone 15 and all older models can run iOS 27, but they do not support Apple Intelligence.


						

							





 FAQ 


1.
When was iOS 27 released?
iOS 27 was released on September 14, 2026.





2.
Which iPhones get iOS 27?
The iPhone 11 and iPhone SE 2 and newer get iOS 27. However, Siri AI and other Apple Intelligence features require iPhone 15 Pro or newer, and the new more expressive Siri voices feature requires iPhone Air, iPhone 17 Pro, or newer.





3.
Which iPhones will get Siri AI and Apple Intelligence in iOS 27?
The only iPhones that can run Siri AI are the iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max and any newer generation. If you have a standard iPhone 15 then you won’t get Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.

title: Apple's Insider Trading Policy Now Covers Prediction Markets
content:
Apple has added an explicit ban on using confidential information to bet on prediction markets to its insider trading policy, according to a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.


The policy was filed on Tuesday as an exhibit to Apple's annual report on Form 10-K, which is also available on Apple's Investor Relations website. The new version is marked "Updated October 2026," while an earlier version that Apple filed in 2024 doesn't mention prediction markets at all.

If you haven't heard of them, prediction markets are basically platforms where people buy and sell contracts that pay out depending on whether a future event happens.

The new clause in Apple's policy is titled "No Trading in Prediction Markets Based on Confidential Information," and it warns employees not to "participate in 'prediction markets' or similar platforms to wager, bet, trade, buy or sell contracts based on the outcome of future events," when doing so involves confidential information obtained through their work at Apple.

It's not a blanket ban, however. The restriction applies only when confidential information is used, but that also includes information about other companies, such as Apple's suppliers, manufacturers, vendors, customers and carrier partners. Apple also says employees must not share confidential information to others who may go on to use it on such markets.

This article, "Apple's Insider Trading Policy Now Covers Prediction Markets" first appeared on MacRumors.com

title: How USB-C drives can change how you use your iPhone
content:
The iPhone 15 family of devices was the first to have USB-C ports, but you really aren't making the most of it if all you do is use yours to charge. Here's what you can do, and what you can't with external drives.


There are SSDs designed especially for use with iPhones.
The beauty of the USB-C port is that there are already countless devices and accessories out there that can plug into it. That's the benefit of a "universal" port, after all.
In the case of your iPhone, being able to charge it using a friend's cable is just the beginning. The real fun starts when you plug things like external storage into it.

title: Everyone is struggling (except Apple)
content:
Macworld





Last week, the Wall Street Journal ran a piece describing how memory and flash chip manufacturers were finally “getting their revenge” on Apple. The demand spike from AI-driven data centers has made it so Apple can no longer negotiate extremely low prices.
Provocative language aside, it’s worth noting that while Apple may indeed be paying a lot more for components, it isn’t exactly hurting here. The company just posted its biggest September quarter of all time. Yes, you would expect revenue to be up with price increases, but Apple’s profit broke records for both the 4th quarter ($30.7 billion) and full year ($132.2 billion) while prices on Macs and iPhones rose to fresh highs.
In other words, everything is more expensive, but Apple is raking it in while you pay more.
Fleecing you on RAM and storage upgrades
The most interesting part of the WSJ story was the data on just how badly we have all been overpaying for Apple’s flash storage upgrades all these years. We’ve noted for a long time that Apple’s prices for upgraded storage on all its products, and RAM on new Macs, are excessive. The WSJ’s research points out just how bad it has been.

				
					

				
			It’s shocking how high the margins used to be for storage upgrades, but they’re still really high today.Wall Street Journal
Last year, Apple charged users between 8 and 12 times more for storage upgrades on the iPhone than its own costs. Sure, the company has margins to protect, but over a thousand percent? This year, with the chip scarcity and higher prices, Apple is only charging you triple what it pays. A bargain!
The article doesn’t break down Apple’s costs and margins on RAM upgrades for Macs over the years, but it’s not much different than flash storage. Apple has charged $400 to increase a MacBook from 16GB to 32GB. Today that may cost Apple as much as $200, but a year ago it was as little as $40. The chip crunch has moved Apple’s margins from “astronomical” to merely “high.”
Passing on the costs
This quarter, Apple’s margins dropped from 50.1 percent last quarter to 47.9 percent (actually closer to 48 and 47, respectively, after adjusting for tariff refunds). Don’t be fooled, Apple’s not really feeling the pinch of these higher component prices.
Apple’s margins are actually up a tiny bit (from 47.2 percent) compared to the same quarter last year, and are way up over time. A decade ago, Apple’s margins were hovering around 38 percent. They’ve dipped down several times in the last few years, too, usually in the fourth quarter, just like this year.

				
					

				
			For a company that largely sells consumer hardware, Apple’s margins are very high and climbing. Don’t let one quarter fool you.Six Colors
In other words, Apple is making a higher profit on more revenue than ever before. While you pay more for every Apple product, the company is protecting its margins, not its profitability. Lower costs were rarely passed on, but higher costs almost always are. It’s like Exxon making billions when the price of oil rises.
To put it in perspective, other huge tech companies with even higher margins are all primarily software and service companies (Microsoft, Meta, Alphabet, and Amazon all enjoy higher margins than Apple). Selling consumer goods carries with it higher costs, so margins are tighter. Apple enjoys much higher margins than consumer tech hardware companies like Samsung (39 percent), Dell (20 percent), Lenovo (15 percent), or Sony (31 percent). Services revenue helps bring the number up (look at how the gross margin rose after Apple TV launched in 2019), but Apple also enjoys higher hardware margins than those other companies.
Looking ahead, Apple expects a gross margin of 45-46 percent for the holiday quarter (Apple’s first quarter of fiscal 2027) and total company revenue to grow between 7 percent and 10 percent year-over-year despite constrained supply. That would give Apple revenue of around $154 billion, an all-time record. Granted, it’s not the 16 percent growth or the 48.2 percent gross margin it saw last year, but it’s hardly a hardship. 
The truth is, Apple is looking out for its real customers–the investors. It repurchased $86 billion in stock this fiscal year, including $24 billion last quarter, a practice that started in 2024 under Tim Cook and will almost certainly continue under Ternus. When Apple pays more for components, it raises your prices instead of cutting back on stock buybacks or lowering margins. The share price is king. So enjoy your $2,499 2TB iPhone.

title: macOS 27 Golden Gate: What’s new, what’s in the beta & what’s next
content:
Macworld





macOS 27 Golden Gate arrived on September 14, introducing an all-new Siri AI assistant, major updates to Safari, Photos, Messages, Mail and Calendar, and expanded child-safety features. Design refinements and performance improvements round out the release.
Named after California’s iconic Golden Gate, the update continues Apple’s push to make the Mac smarter and more proactive, bringing Apple Intelligence to more parts of the operating system to help users complete everyday tasks faster.
macOS 27 supports all Macs powered by Apple silicon, but drops support for Intel-based models. Intel Macs can continue running older versions of macOS, with security updates expected to remain available for a limited time.
This guide covers macOS 27’s biggest new features, compatible Macs and the latest beta developments. We explain what’s available now, which features are being tested and what’s expected in future updates, including when those additions could arrive.


What’s New in macOS 27 Golden Gate at a glance

				
					

				
			
Apple




Here are the top ten new features and changes in macOS 27 Golden Gate.
Siri AI: A redesigned conversational Siri that can answer questions, understand personal and onscreen context, access the web and take actions across apps.
Apple Intelligence: Systemwide proofreading, smarter writing tools, improved dictation and automatic file and folder naming.
Safari upgrades: Automatic tab grouping, webpage change alerts with Notify Me, AI-generated extensions and faster, more efficient browsing.
Smarter Messages and Mail: Better search and syncing, contextual suggestions and improved reliability.
New Photos tools: Spatial Reframing, image expansion with Extend, improved Clean Up, and better search and organization.
More powerful built-in apps: New features for Passwords, Calendar, Notes, Preview, Freeform, Weather, Shortcuts, and Image Playground.
Expanded parental controls: Ask to Browse, improved Screen Time, contact approvals and broader Communication Safety protections.
Better Mac gaming: Game Porting Toolkit 4 promises significant performance and compatibility improvements for Windows games.
Refined Liquid Glass design: Better readability and consistency, adjustable transparency, cleaner Finder windows, and improved iPhone Mirroring.
Faster macOS performance: Quicker app launches, Spotlight, AirDrop and networking, plus improved external-display, Thunderbolt and Bluetooth support.



							


macOS 27 latest version: What’s in macOS 27.2
macOS 27 became available to install on compatible Macs on September 14.
Apple released macOS 27.2 on October 26, 2026. Alongside bug fixes and security updates, it adds:
Better Siri context: Siri can recall earlier conversations and use additional information, including Messages photo attachments, Calendar attendees and voicemails, with improved results from Safari history and Reading List.
Excluded Apps: One setting controls which apps Siri, Search and suggestions can access.
Write with Siri in Mail: Access it from the message-composition formatting bar.
Messages Suggestions: Turn conversation details into actions in Calendar and Reminders.
Shared Albums improvements: Edit captions and comments, avoid duplicate photos and receive expiry reminders.
SynthID support: Identify AI-generated or modified images in Photos and Image Playground.
Podcasts changes: Separate sections for new episodes and unfinished listening.
FaceTime accessibility: Add a third-party sign-language interpreter or live captioner


						

							


Latest macOS 27 Beta
macOS 27.3 developer beta

				
					

				
			

Apple




Apple released the first macOS 27.3 developer beta on November 3, 2026. The beta update introduces new Safari features, including vertical tabs, Adaptive Dark Mode and additional Siri browser controls, which Apple is testing before the full release in macOS 27.3, all being well. 
Want to run the beta? Here’s how you can participate in the beta program we also recommend reading our guide to whether you should install the latest macOS beta. Beta software can cause crashes, app compatibility problems, increased battery drain and, in some cases, data loss. If you install a beta, make a full backup first and, ideally, use a secondary Mac, separate volume or external SSD.


						

							


What features are still to come in macOS 27
At the time of the launch of macOS 27 not all of Apple’s promised features were available. Some new features arrived in macOS 27.2, but there are still missing features, including:
Automatic password changes: The ability for the Passwords app to visit supported websites and automatically replace compromised passwords was removed shortly before release. 


						

							


macOS 27 problems: Are there any issues with Golden Gate?
Since macOS 27 Golden Gate arrived on Macs there have been reports in the Apple Support Community of issues with Mission Control and Spaces. 
These include: 
Stuttering or delayed transitions: Reports long pauses before a new Space appears. 
Black or missing desktop previews: A black screen may appear when switching Spaces. 
French website MacGeneration was able to reproduce some Mission Control glitches. 


						

							


Siri AI: Siri powered macOS 27 features  

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Apple’s biggest focus in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Siri AI, a completely redesigned version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence. Rather than functioning primarily as a voice assistant, Siri is now a conversational AI that can answer questions, understand personal and onscreen context, access current information from the web and take actions across apps.
Siri AI behaves more like a generative-AI chatbot than the Siri of old. It can answer questions directly, understand natural follow-ups and solve problems instead of simply directing users to web searches.
At a glance: What’s new with Siri AI?
Conversational AI assistant: Siri can handle open-ended questions, brainstorming, research and natural back-and-forth conversations.
Dedicated Siri app: A standalone Siri app keeps conversations in one place and syncs them through iCloud, allowing users to start a conversation on one Apple device and continue it on another.
Personal context awareness: Siri can understand information in Messages, Mail, Notes, Photos, Maps and files to locate information and provide answers based on your personal data.
Web-powered answers: Siri can access current information from the web, making it more useful for research, learning, interview preparation and questions about recent events.
App actions and automation: Siri can perform tasks across apps such as Messages, Music, Reminders, Calendar and Maps using natural-language instructions.
Spotlight integration: Siri AI is integrated with Spotlight, allowing users to type questions and receive AI-generated answers without opening a browser or separate app.
Visual Intelligence: Visual Intelligence comes to the Mac for the first time, allowing Siri to understand selected images, documents, files, text and other content displayed on screen.

				
					

				
			
Apple’s Visual Intelligence initially placed Blutenburg in Denmark.

Macwelt





Writing Tools: Siri can generate text, rewrite drafts, summarise content and adjust wording or tone. Apple says it can also adapt writing to the way you typically communicate with particular contacts.
Improved dictation: Systemwide dictation gains better speech recognition along with automatic punctuation, capitalization and formatting.
Custom Siri voices: Users can choose Siri’s voice and adjust characteristics such as pace and expressiveness, although some of these capabilities require newer hardware.
A Siri AI contextural popover was discovered during beta testing. Selecting text brings up a small Siri icon offering contextual actions, including Writing Tools, summaries and key points, sending messages or emails, creating calendar events, opening locations in Maps, and tracking flights or packages. However, the feature is not enabled by default and requires Apple’s FeatureFlags system to activate. It remains unclear whether Apple intends to make it available as a consumer-facing feature. 
Apple also appears to be taking a relatively restrained approach to AI behaviour. In our testing, Siri avoids presenting itself as human, excessive flattery and potentially harmful responses, while generally keeping its answers straightforward.
Siri AI has launched as a beta, so users should expect some rough edges and continued improvements.
With macOS 27.2, Siri AI supports French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish in addition to English. Availability will vary by region. Siri AI is available on Mac and Vision Pro in the European Union, although Siri AI remains unavailable on iPhone and iPad in the EU at launch because of issues related to the Digital Markets Act. It is also unavailable in mainland China while Apple works through regulatory requirements.
Which Macs support Siri AI?
Siri AI requires a Mac that supports Apple Intelligence, but some of its most advanced capabilities have higher hardware requirements. Apple says its most powerful on-device AI model, expressive Siri voices and advanced dictation require an M3 or later Mac with at least 12GB of unified memory. Macs that support Apple Intelligence but do not meet those requirements can still receive other Siri AI features, although the exact feature set may vary.



							


Safari features in macOS 27

				
					

				
			
Notify Me in Safari

Apple




Safari gets several Apple Intelligence-powered upgrades in macOS 27, including smarter tab organization, webpage monitoring, custom extension generation, and performance improvements.
Automatic Tab Topics: Safari automatically groups related tabs by topic as you browse, helping keep research and projects organized. These groups can also be saved for later.
Notify Me: Safari can monitor webpages for changes and alert you when something happens, such as a product coming back in stock or a price dropping, removing the need to keep refreshing pages manually.
Describe an Extension: Users can create custom Safari extensions simply by describing what they want. Safari generates the extension from the text description and add it to the toolbar.
Faster, more efficient browsing: Apple says Safari uses less power while improving page-loading speed, JavaScript performance, scrolling, animations and resizing of the Start Page.

				
					

				
			
Get notified. 

Macwelt




Safari features coming in macOS 27.3
The macOS 27.3 developer beta adds three new Safari features:
Vertical tabs: Open tabs can appear down the left side of the browser window. They initially appear as icons, but you can widen the sidebar to display their titles.
Adaptive Dark Mode: Safari can apply a dark appearance to websites that don’t offer their own dark mode. You can enable it automatically or choose which sites use it.
Siri browser controls: On compatible Macs, Siri can perform tasks such as clearing Safari’s cache and organizing tabs.
These features are currently only available for developer beta testers. Read more about Safari’s new features in macOS 27.3.


						

							


Messages and Mail features in macOS 27
Messages and Mail gain deeper Apple Intelligence integration in macOS 27, alongside improvements to search, syncing and everyday reliability.
Messages
Suggestions in Messages (added in macOS 27.2): Messages suggests actions based on your conversation, such as creating a Calendar event for dinner plans or adding a reminder.
Smarter Photo Suggestions: Messages surfaces relevant photos based on people, places and keywords mentioned in a conversation.
Personalized Smart Reply: During the preview at WWDC Apple indicated that suggested replies can reflect your usual writing style and adapt depending on who you’re messaging. This was removed from the iOS 27 beta before launch and hasn’t arrived with macOS 27. 
Improved syncing: Messages should sync more reliably across devices, while failed messages automatically retry sending.
Mail
Personalized Smart Reply: Apple also previewed a feature in Mail whereby it could generates suggested responses that better match your writing style and the person you’re replying to, but this is absent from the first version of macOS 27. 
More relevant search: A new ranking system prioritizes the most useful search results, alongside improved search indexing.
Faster and more accurate: Apple says Mail loads messages more quickly and provide more reliable unread counts.


						

							


Photos features in macOS 27
Photos has new AI-powered editing and organization tools in macOS 27, making it easier to improve images, find photos and manage an iCloud library.
Spatial Reframing: Photos will intelligently recompose and reframe images after they’ve been taken.
Extend Tool: A new Extend tool can expand an image beyond its original boundaries, filling in missing areas when changing the crop or aspect ratio.
Enhanced Clean Up: Apple’s Clean Up tool is better at removing larger unwanted objects and distractions from photos.
Better organisation and search: Photos adds keywords, star ratings, improved metadata search and other tools for organising a library.
Faster iCloud syncing: iCloud Photos can begin uploads more quickly, with an option to prioritize syncing when needed.


						

							


Other new app features in macOS 27
macOS 27 also brings a wide range of smaller upgrades across Apple’s built-in apps, with a particular focus on automation, organisation, security and Apple Intelligence.
Passwords
In macOS 27 the Passwords app will automatically identify weak or compromised passwords and, with Apple Intelligence, visit supported websites, change the password and save the new credentials. This could remove much of the manual work involved in updating large numbers of old or leaked passwords, although questions remain over website compatibility, two-factor authentication and how consistently the feature will work. Read: Apple finally got rid of my biggest password headache. 
This feature was not included in the initial macOS 27 release and may arrive in a subsequent update. 
Image Playground
Image Playground gets a substantial AI upgrade, including the ability to create photorealistic images and make more convincing edits to existing pictures, such as changing colours, hair and other details. Apple continues to apply safeguards around real people, copyrighted characters and distinctive artistic styles. macOS 27.2 added SynthID support for images generated or modified using Photos and Image Playground.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Calendar
Calendar gains natural-language event creation, making it possible to describe an event rather than manually entering every detail. It can also make changes to multiple events at once.
Preview
Preview supports more document formats, improves PDF editing and saves PDF files more quickly.
Notes
Notes gains drawing tools for sketching with a mouse or trackpad, along with digital signatures, Markdown copy-and-paste and links to sections within notes.

				
					

				
			
Notes now features a drawing tool as well as the ability to create and use digital signatures.

Foundry




Freeform
Freeform adds drawing tools, collaborative folders and improved organisation, including the ability to sort boards into folders. Full dark-mode support also changes the appearance of the drawing canvas.

				
					

				
			
In Freeform, boards can now be organised into folders.

Foundry




Weather
Weather gets a clearer and more detailed forecast interface, with reorganised information tiles and enhanced 10-day forecasts showing precipitation probability and amount, as well as wind speeds throughout the day.

				
					

				
			
In the Weather app, the tiles have been rearranged, and there are separate 10-day forecasts for precipitation and wind (circled in red).

Foundry




Shortcuts
Shortcuts gains a redesigned editor, more automation capabilities and one of macOS 27’s more ambitious AI features: the ability to turn natural-language instructions into working automations.

				
					

				
			Shortcuts can start automatically when a specific event occurs.

Thomas Armbrüster




Parental Controls
Apple expands its family-safety tools with Safari’s Ask to Browse, improved Screen Time and Time Allowances, contact approvals, and broader Communication Safety protections. The changes give parents more control over what children can access and who they can communicate with without completely locking down the Mac.
The redesigned parental controls also have a family-wide software requirement. To activate them through Family Sharing, every eligible device in the group – not just the parent’s Mac – must be running iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27 or visionOS 27.
Once Apple offers the migration, the family organizer or a parent or guardian should see a Get Started prompt in Family settings. Apple says parents can also select the child’s name under System Settings > Family to begin setup, although the migration options are not currently appearing for everyone.
Older devices that cannot install version 27 can continue using the previous Screen Time and Family Sharing controls. Apple says these legacy devices should not prevent supported hardware from using the redesigned system, but it has acknowledged delays and incorrect device-status information affecting some families..
Accessibility, Shared Albums and Suggestions
macOS 27 also includes accessibility improvements, expanded Shared Albums, and more contextual Suggestions throughout the operating system.
Game Porting Toolkit 4
Apple’s Game Porting Toolkit 4 arrives alongside macOS 27 and promises significant improvements for running and porting Windows games on Apple silicon Macs. Early beta testing suggests substantial performance gains. On an M4 Pro MacBook Pro, GTA V reportedly increased from around 106fps to 176fps, while Red Dead Redemption 2 improved from roughly 60fps to 75fps.
The results suggest software compatibility, rather than raw Apple silicon performance, is increasingly the main obstacle to better Mac gaming. Improvements to Game Porting Toolkit could make Windows titles more practical to run and easier for developers to bring to macOS.


						

							


Design and Interface Changes in macOS 27

				
					

				
			
Apple




macOS 27 Golden Gate refines the Liquid Glass redesign introduced in macOS 26, with Apple focusing on readability, consistency and usability rather than another major visual overhaul.
Changes include:
Improved Liquid Glass: Stronger contrast, better readability and more consistent refraction effects across windows, menus and controls.
Customizable transparency: Users can adjust the Liquid Glass effect in System Settings, from a clearer appearance to a more heavily tinted look.
Cleaner Finder and toolbars: Finder sidebars are more clearly defined, toolbars are more consistent, and edge-to-edge sidebars replace some of the floating elements introduced in macOS 26.
More consistent windows: Window corners, controls and active-window highlighting have been standardized to make the interface feel more coherent.
Updated icons and menus: Menu-bar and app icons gain sharper outlines, improved contrast and more depth, while unnecessary menu icons have been reduced.
Smoother window management: Mission Control and Spaces animations have been refined, and active windows should be easier to distinguish.
New wallpapers and screensavers: Golden Gate-themed backgrounds include animated daytime and nighttime views of the bridge.
Swipe to refresh: Supported Mac apps gain a swipe-down-to-refresh gesture.
Improved iPhone Mirroring: iPhone Mirroring adds Control Center access, resizable app windows and support for DRM-protected video.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Touch on Mac: How macOS works with a touchscreen
macOS 27 supports direct touchscreen input on the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display. Touch works alongside the keyboard and trackpad, giving you another way to interact with apps rather than replacing the controls you already use.
You can swipe to scroll through webpages, pinch to zoom into photos, and drag content between documents. Window gestures include double-tapping to fill the screen and flicking a window to tile it into place. Apple says many existing apps work immediately because macOS translates touches into mouse clicks, while developers can use updated gesture APIs to build more specialized touch controls.
Apple has also announced touch-focused updates for creative apps. Examples include playing onscreen instruments in Logic Pro and selecting ranges, placing clips and zooming into edits in Final Cut Pro. These app updates are scheduled for November.
Direct touchscreen input requires compatible hardware: the 14-inch or 16-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display. 


						

							


Performance improvements and system changes in macOS 27
Apple says macOS 27 focuses on speed, efficiency and everyday usability, with improvements across apps, networking, displays and system tasks. Most of these changes do not require Apple Intelligence.
Changes include:
Faster overall performance: Apps should launch more quickly, while an optimized CPU scheduler improves system responsiveness.
Faster Spotlight and setup: Spotlight indexing and new user-account creation are quicker.
Faster file transfers and networking: AirDrop and network file browsing are faster, while Ethernet status can appear in the menu bar.
Thunderbolt and Bluetooth improvements: RDMA over Thunderbolt has been improved, alongside more efficient Bluetooth power management.
Faster Safari: The Safari Start Page loads more quickly, with broader browser performance improvements.
Better external-display support: New high-resolution and high-refresh-rate modes include 5K at 120Hz, alongside improved display-position persistence, HDR support for the macOS interface and 5K Mac mirroring.
Apple Intelligence powered changes:
AI-powered file naming – requires Apple Intelligence: macOS can suggest filenames and folder names based on their contents, including in Pages, Numbers, TextEdit and Finder.
Systemwide proofreading – requires Apple Intelligence: Apple Intelligence provides automatic proofreading and improved spelling and grammar suggestions throughout macOS.
Apple Intelligence privacy: Apple says AI processing happens on-device where possible, with Private Cloud Compute used for more demanding tasks. Data processed in the cloud is not stored or made accessible to Apple.


						

							


macOS 27 Compatible Macs 

				
					

				
			
The MacBook Neo and other Macs in Apple’s current lineup will all be compatible with macOS 27.

Foundry




Apple states that macOS 27 Golden Gate is compatible with:
MacBook Neo (A18 Pro, 2026)
MacBook Air (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
MacBook Pro (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
iMac (Apple silicon, 2021 and later)
Mac mini (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
Mac Studio (2022 and later)
Mac Pro (Apple silicon, 2023 and later)
All supported Macs can run Apple Intelligence, although some of the most advanced Siri AI features require an M3 or later Mac with at least 12GB of unified memory.
What about Intel Macs?
macOS 27 marks another major step in Apple’s transition away from Intel. macOS 26 Tahoe was the final version to support Intel Macs, and Apple is now encouraging developers to remove Intel code from their apps and focus on Apple silicon.
macOS 27 will also be the final version to support Rosetta, Apple’s translation technology for running Intel-only apps on Apple silicon Macs. Those apps will continue to work in macOS 27, but will stop working in macOS 28 unless developers release Apple silicon-native versions.
To help users prepare, macOS 27 includes an Intel-app checker in System Settings that lists Intel-based apps used during the past year. If you still rely on any essential Intel-only software, now is a good time to look for updates or alternatives before upgrading to macOS 28.
What happens to DVD support?
macOS 27 also begins the phase-out of Apple’s native DVD support. Apple has removed the DVDPlayback framework from the macOS 27 SDK and says it will disappear completely in a future version of macOS.
Golden Gate may still include the DVD Player app, but it is likely to be the last macOS release with Apple’s built-in DVD playback support. Users who still watch DVDs on a Mac will increasingly need to rely on third-party software such as VLC.


						

							





 FAQ 


1.
When was macOS 27 Golden Gate released?
September 14, 2026.





2.
Should I install macOS 27?
Golden Gate builds on macOS 26 Tahoe rather than reinventing macOS all over again. The biggest changes come from Siri AI and Apple Intelligence, alongside improvements to Safari, Spotlight, Photos, parental controls, and everyday system performance.
But how much has actually changed since macOS 26 Tahoe, and is macOS 27 worth installing? We have a separate article that explains how Golden Gate compares with macOS Tahoe and which Macs will benefit most from upgrading.






3.
Which Macs can run macOS 27?
All M-series Macs can run macOS 27, and the MacBook Neo.
Certain Siri AI features – most powerful on-device model, expressive voices and advanced dictation – are only available for M3 Macs and newer.





4.
Should Intel Mac owners upgrade now?
Intel Mac owners should start planning a move to Apple silicon, particularly if they want macOS 27, Apple Intelligence or continued access to the latest Mac features. The transition away from Intel hardware has reached a critical turning point, with software support rapidly vanishing and a new generation of affordable entry-level hardware making the switch more accessible than ever.
Apple has confirmed that macOS 27 will not support any Intel-based Macs. While a small number of Intel models may receive security patches for older versions of macOS until September 2028, they are already excluded from modern flagship features.
Those with Intel Macs also miss out on many features, including Apple Intelligence.





5.
Will macOS 27 support Rosetta and Intel apps?
macOS 27 will run Intel-only Mac apps through Rosetta 2. However, macOS 27 will be the final version of macOS to support Rosetta 2 as a general-purpose translation technology for running Intel-based Mac apps on Apple silicon.
Rosetta has acted as a transition layer since Apple introduced its own Mac chips in 2020, translating x86_64 Intel instructions so older software can run on Apple silicon. After macOS 27, most Intel-only Mac apps will no longer work unless developers release Apple silicon-native versions, although Apple will retain limited Rosetta functionality for some older, unmaintained games.
Apple is already preparing users for the change. Since macOS 26.4, Macs can display warnings when launching apps that rely on Rosetta, encouraging users (and the app developers) to update to Apple silicon-native versions before general Rosetta support ends.
In macOS 28, most Intel-only apps will no longer run unless developers update them for Apple silicon.





6.
When is macOS usually updated?
Here is a history of release dates for macOS:
macOS 27 Golden Gate: September 14, 2026
macOS 26 Tahoe: September 15, 2025

title: iPhone Duo review: The best and worst iPhone in ages
content:
Macworld





At a glance
Expert's Rating



Pros
Duo-optimized apps change how you use your iPhone
The nano-texture display is great
No real compromise on performance
Cons
Unoptimized apps are worse than on previous iPhones
Battery life varies widely based on inner/outer display use
Cameras are a step behind recent flagship iPhones
Touch ID can be annoying
Our Verdict 
Folding phones come with some inherent tradeoffs, but even so, the iPhone Duo is hard to recommend right now. It simply requires optimized apps to provide a good experience, and there aren’t nearly enough of those. 
Price When Reviewed
